question.prompt: You need to find all pairs in an unsorted array that sum to target k. Which approach gives O(n) time and O(n) space?
choices: Hash map storing complements seen so far
Binary search for each element's complement
question.expectedAnswer: Hash map storing complements seen so far
question.explanation: Frozen author record for a compatibility diagnostic; teaching feedback is assessed separately.

solution.answer:
Use a hash map. In one pass, for each element x check whether the map already contains (k − x); if so, record/count the pair. Then insert x (or increment its frequency) in the map. Each lookup and insert is O(1) expected, so the scan is O(n) time with O(n) space for the map. Important caveat: O(n) time covers detecting that pairs exist and finding distinct-value pairs. If you must enumerate every (i,j) pair, the output itself can be Θ(n²) (e.g., n zeros, target 0 yields n(n−1)/2 pairs), so total work is O(n + number of output pairs). The O(n) guarantee applies only when the output size is O(n) or you just need existence/count per distinct complement.
The O(n) time bound assumes average-case O(1) hash operations; worst-case hash collisions can degrade to O(n) per operation. Additionally, enumerating all index pairs is output-sensitive and can exceed O(n).
